chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad informed me, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAlī ibn Abī al-Mughīrah, from Muyassir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
"Wudu (ablution) is one," and he described the ankle bone as being on the top of the foot.

key_terms.الْكَعْبَ: the ankle bone referred to in legal discussion of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before acts of worship
key_terms.وَاحِدٌ: one; indicating a single prescribed form

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the prescribed form of wudu (ablution) and the location of the ankle?
ai.summary: This hadith states the singular prescribed manner of wudu (ablution) and includes a description of the ankle location relevant to its legal understanding. It is significant in discussions of ritual purity and the jurisprudential details of how wudu (ablution) is to be performed.
